::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 20th 1880  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Devon Record Office, Exeter 53/10/9/3
:::

Dear Madam

I am today sending your book to [Macmillans](organizations/other_111.qmd) 29 and 30 Bedford Street, Covent Garden, and asking if they can give you one of my books to illustrate.  It might be a good plan for you to call there, tomorrow or next day.  Send up your card and ask for [Mr Craik](people/person_379.qmd) or [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd), mentioning my name.

If you cannot call, write, and say how the book shall be returned asking if they can give you a commission to do some illustrations.

After that I will write to [Marcus Ward](organizations/other_236.qmd), who deals more in illustrations, and is going to publish the Bear and the Goblin in a book of poetry[^1]

yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Francis Dawson, 'The Bear and the Goblin' was included in CMY's anthology *Aunt Charlotte's Evenings at Home with the Poets* (London: Marcus Ward 1881).  Perhaps it was one of the texts the unknown woman had illustrated.
